speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hemorrhagic Edema of Infancy (or IgA Vasculitis given the age and presentation). Given the patient is 8 years old, this presentation is highly suggestive of IgA Vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein Purpura) triggered by a recent infection, rather than the drug reaction initially suspected. The rash description (antecubital/popliteal fossae, sparing palms/soles implied by distribution) combined with joint pain and recent sinusitis fits this pattern. I am ready to finalize the diagnosis if you confirm if there is any abdominal pain or hematuria.
